messages:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH severity — Dedicated pool dpool-prod-us-east-1 p99 latency > 5s for streaming endpoints (alerts: latency_p99 > 5s for 5m)

samir (oncall): I got paged — grabbing context. Is this across models or one shard?

jess (eng-sre): seeing it across multiple model routes: chat-streaming and text-gen with large-seq. p95 ~ 1.1s, p99 ~ 6.2s right now.

samir (oncall): thanks. any correlation with autoscaler logs?

taylor (eng-runtime): autoscaler shows scale-up attempts for dpool-prod-us-east-1 at 4312095600, handshake/warmup delays ~ 90s, many warmups aborted. Pool capacity at 97%.

jess (eng-sre): queue depth spiked: ~8200 inflight requests queued for dedicated route. backlog is causing tail latency on streaming (stall on initial tokens).

samir (oncall): customer impact? high-level?

mia (prod-safety): multiple mid-market customers reporting timeouts > 10s for streaming responses, a couple of sessions dropped. No data plane errors, just long stalls.

ops-bot: Metric snapshot: 
- dpool-prod-us-east-1 utilization: 97%
- queue_depth: 8200
- warmup_success_rate (last 5m): 42%
- autoscale_retries: 3
- model_variant_fallbacks: 0

samir (oncall): going to follow runbook triage. First action: enable fallback routing to lower-capacity model variant for non-enterprise customers. taylor, can you trigger temporary routing rule?\

taylor (eng-runtime): on it. pushing rule to route match: route.metadata.tier != "enterprise" -> model=redwood-small-quantized. ETA ~ 90s for rollout via config service.

jess (eng-sre): also we should reduce batch windows for streaming to keep per-request latency lower. I'm toggling batch.max_wait_ms from 50 -> 10 for this pool.

samir (oncall): approved. jess, note any side effects.

jess (eng-sre): batch change applied to dpool-prod-us-east-1. Observability: immediate drop in batching, but throughput per-GPU drops ~10%. Acceptable short-term.

mia (prod-safety): notify support for customers with sessions > 30s. I'll draft a short inbound message.

ops-bot: Config rollout complete: fallback routing applied (non-enterprise). Batch window updated.

taylor (eng-runtime): seeing warmup handshake still failing for some nodes — handshake timeout 60s configured; logs show NVidia driver warnings on 3 machines, GPU INIT slow. Suspect hardware flakiness interfering with scale-up.

jess (eng-sre): can we mark those hosts as draining? which hosts?

taylor (eng-runtime): hosts: gpuhost-12, gpuhost-15, gpuhost-18. Draining now. New scale attempts will avoid them.

samir (oncall): good. after drain, autoscaler should bring new healthy instances up. How long to rebuild capacity?\

taylor (eng-runtime): cold pool creation + warmup ~ 3-4m once scheduler assigns. BUT warmup success is currently flaky due to the failed warmup path — KV cache priming step failing intermittently. Investigating.

jess (eng-sre): while that's happening, I'm going to temporarily increase routing to hosted fallback (hosted-prod-1) for 10% of traffic for enterprise customers to avoid SLA impact. Needs exec sign-off? This is an emergency mitigation.

samir (oncall): do it. prioritize customer-facing stability. Documenting in incident ticket.

mia (prod-safety): alert messages queued to support: "We are investigating degraded streaming performance; temporary mitigations applied. We'll update in 30 minutes." :warning:

ops-bot: Telemetry 5m after mitigations: 
- p95: 0.9s -> 0.8s
- p99: 6.2s -> 2.4s
- queue_depth: 8200 -> 1900
- streaming stalls rate: -70%

samir (oncall): that's promising. root cause still looks like a mix of pool saturation + a subset of GPUs failing warmup, causing autoscaler retries and delayed capacity.

taylor (eng-runtime): confirmed. root cause hypothesis: a recent kernel/driver roll triggered on gpuhost-12/15/18 causing slow device init and occasional hangs of warmup agent. Rollout correlates with host timestamps.

jess (eng-sre): plan: 1) keep fallback routing in place until pool healthy, 2) set warmup handshake timeout to 120s to avoid aborts while we restart drivers, 3) drain + rebuild the three hosts, 4) monitor p99 and queue.

samir (oncall): agree. assign tasks: taylor - driver restart + drain/gpu-rebuild; jess - adjust warmup timeout and monitor queues; mia - customer comms; I'll keep incident ownership and escalate to infra on-call if rebuilds take > 15m.

taylor (eng-runtime): starting driver restart on gpuhost-12 now. I'll mark progress here.

(5m later)

taylor (eng-runtime): gpuhost-12 driver restart done, warmup handshake for new nodes succeeding. gpuhost-15 restart queued.

ops-bot: Metric update: queue_depth 1900 -> 900, p99 2.4s -> 1.3s.

samir (oncall): good. Mia, please escalate any enterprise support tickets we should proactively reach out to.

mia (prod-safety): flagged two Tier-1 accounts; support sent heads-up and will follow-up in 15m with status.

(25m later)

jess (eng-sre): warmup_timeout increased to 120s. Autoscaler logs show fewer aborted warmups. New pool capacity restored to 93%.

taylor (eng-runtime): gpuhost-15 and 18 rebuilt, all three healthy and back in rotation. Warmup success rate 98% now.

ops-bot: End-state metrics: 
- pool utilization: 85%
- queue_depth: 120
- p95: 0.6s
- p99: 0.9s
- streaming stalls: baseline

samir (oncall): closing the live mitigation phase. Fallback routing will be removed in 10m unless we see regressions. I'll start a short post-incident doc and assign root cause follow-ups: driver rollout gating, warmup timeout tuning, autoscaler backoff parameters.

mia (prod-safety): prepping customer postmortem note.

jess (eng-sre): tagging infra and runtime to review the driver rollout process.

samir (oncall): handing off to jess (eng-sre) for post-incident follow-ups. jess — you're the incident lead for the writeup.

jess (eng-sre): acknowledged. Taking over. Oncall Handoff -> jess (eng-sre).

samir (oncall): thanks team. Closing thread in 30m after final checks. :thumbsup:
